name: throughline
description: Give Claude complete understanding of your software project.
long_description: Throughline indexes a local repository — files, symbols, imports, call graph, git history and documentation — and exposes it to Claude as a set of precise retrieval tools. Ask conceptual questions ("where is rate limiting handled?"), trace execution paths, find every caller before a rename, review repository health, or generate architecture and onboarding documentation grounded in the actual code. Everything runs on your machine: source code is read locally, indexed into a local SQLite database inside your project, and never uploaded anywhere by this extension.

workspace_roots.title: Project directories
workspace_roots.description: Directories this connector may read. Choosing a directory here is what grants access; nothing outside these paths is ever read.

allow_writes.title: Allow writing generated documentation
allow_writes.description: When off, the connector can only read. When on, write_documentation can save a generated file — and still requires explicit confirmation on every write.

max_files.title: Maximum files to index
max_files.description: Safety limit for very large directories. Indexing stops here and tells you the index is incomplete.

log_level.title: Log level
log_level.description: Diagnostic verbosity on stderr. Use debug when reporting a problem.

tools.name: list_workspaces
tools.description: Lists the workspace directories this connector may read, and whether each has been indexed. Resolves which project is meant when several are granted.

tools.name: scan_repository
tools.description: Builds or rebuilds the searchable index for a workspace: files, symbols, imports, call edges, git history and documentation.

tools.name: refresh_index
tools.description: Updates the index for files that changed since the last run. Much faster than scan_repository. Use this when the user has edited code during the conversation.

tools.name: search_code
tools.description: Finds code by meaning as well as by name.

tools.name: find_symbol
tools.description: Locates a definition by name. Use when the user names a specific function, class, type or constant. Faster and more precise than search_code for exact identifiers.

tools.name: find_references
tools.description: Lists everywhere a symbol is called or referenced, with call sites. Use before renaming or deleting anything, and to understand how a function is actually used.

tools.name: explain_file
tools.description: Summarises one file: what it defines, what it imports, what imports it, and its recent change history. Use when the user asks what a file does or opens an unfamiliar one.

tools.name: explain_symbol
tools.description: Gives full context for one symbol: signature, documentation, what it calls, what calls it, and where it sits in the architecture.

tools.name: trace_execution
tools.description: Traces the call path between two symbols, or outward from one. Use for "what happens when a request hits this endpoint" and for understanding how a value reaches a destination.

tools.name: project_overview
tools.description: High-level orientation for a codebase: size, languages, frameworks, entry points, layer structure and key documentation.

tools.name: dependency_graph
tools.description: Renders the import graph as Mermaid, either for the whole workspace or around one file. Aggregates to directories when the file count is too large to read.

tools.name: architecture_diagram
tools.description: Produces a Mermaid diagram of the codebase: layer view, folder tree or change hotspots. Use to give the user a visual anchor when explaining structure.

tools.name: list_entry_points
tools.description: Lists where execution starts: HTTP routes, CLI commands, background workers, scheduled jobs and main functions. Use to answer "how does anything get called here?".

tools.name: recent_changes
tools.description: Summarises recent commit activity: what changed, who changed it, and which files are churning. Use to catch up on a project or to find who to ask about an area.

tools.name: repository_health
tools.description: Reports possible dead code, unused dependencies, import cycles, complexity spikes, untested modules and unresolved imports.

tools.name: find_dead_code
tools.description: Lists non-exported symbols with no resolved references — candidates for deletion.

tools.name: draft_documentation
tools.description: Assembles a documentation draft — README, architecture overview or onboarding guide — from the index and returns it as text. Never touches the filesystem.

tools.name: write_documentation
tools.description: Writes a generated documentation file into the workspace, overwriting any existing file at that path. Writes the same content draft_documentation returns.
